title: Option Deposit Refund and Forfeiture When a Purchase Agreement Ends — Design Studio Selections
content:
When the purchase agreement is cancelled or terminated the Design Studio Selections file is cancelled on the same date. Option deposits are then refunded according to the cancellation basis recorded on the purchase agreement's cancellation request and the file status when the agreement ended.

| Cancellation basis on the request | File status when the agreement ended | Refund percent |
|---|---|---|
| Rescission or builder delay | Any | The package's refund percent for rescission or builder delay |
| Any other buyer cancellation | Before structural close (awaiting appointment or in selection) | The package's refund percent before structural close |
| Any other buyer cancellation | After structural close (structural closed or finalized) | The package's refund percent after structural close |
| Termination for buyer default | Any | The package's refund percent after structural close |

**Computation.** Each refund and each forfeiture is computed per source payment — each option deposit payment by its receipt number — as the payment amount multiplied by the refund percent, rounded half up to the cent; the forfeited part is the remainder of that payment. Refunds follow the purchase agreement's refund timing.

**Worked figures (hypothetical inputs, refund percent 75)**

| Receipt | Amount paid | Refund (75 percent, rounded half up) | Forfeited remainder |
|---|---|---|---|
| First payment | 1234.57 | 925.93 | 308.64 |
| Second payment | 500.00 | 375.00 | 125.00 |

The first refund is 1234.57 multiplied by 75 percent, that is 925.9275, rounded to 925.93; the forfeited part is 1234.57 less 925.93.

**Question answered by the rule**

*Are the two payments added together before the percent is applied?* No. Each refund and forfeiture is computed and rounded per source payment.
